svg.text: Breastfeeding problems are nearly always attachment problems
Watch a feed before you advise on one
Good attachment looks like this
Mouth wide open, chin pressed into the breast
Lower lip turned outwards
More dark skin visible above than below
Slow deep sucks with pauses, and swallowing
you can hear
The mother feels tugging, not pain
Poor attachment and what it produces
Nipple pain and cracks — the baby is on the
nipple instead of the breast
Rapid shallow sucking, clicking sounds
Engorgement, then blocked ducts, then mastitis
A baby feeding constantly and still hungry
and a mother told her milk is “not enough”
The measurement that answers “is my milk enough?”
Weight gain over time, and wet nappies — six or more heavy ones in twenty-four hours
Not: how long she feeds, how the breast feels, or whether milk can be expressed by hand
A soft breast in an established feeder is normal, not empty
Engorgement versus mastitis
Engorged: both breasts, tight and tender,
no fever — feed more often, not less
Mastitis: one wedge-shaped red area, fever,
and she must keep feeding from that breast
What quietly ends exclusive feeding
Water “because of the heat” — breast milk is
already mostly water and displaces feeds
Herbal preparations, a bottle at night, and
a grandmother who was told porridge at three months
